prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title: 'ITP: immune recognition and clearance'. A horizontal visual sequence of exactly three large stages without rectangular boxes: left one small purple oval platelet, centre the same platelet with six simple teal rounded antibody-marker tabs (not molecular Y shapes) attached to its OUTER SURFACE, right one much larger soft coral C-shaped abstract immune-clearance symbol gently enclosing that tagged platelet. Do not draw a realistic cell, nucleus, organ, spleen or blood vessel. The C shape is a conceptual engulfment icon only, with no cell organelles. Navy arrows connect left to centre to right. Labels below: 'Platelet', 'Antibody recognition', 'Immune clearance'. Under the last stage, a small group of three purple platelet dots instead of a larger faint group implies 'Fewer circulating platelets'. Bottom short sentence: 'Reduced production may also contribute'. Use graceful molecular-object composition; no extra claims.

teaching.question: How can immune recognition reduce circulating platelet numbers in ITP?
teaching.answer: Antibodies may coat platelets and promote their removal by immune cells. Reduced platelet production can also contribute.

title: Immune recognition and platelet clearance
caption: Antibodies can mark platelets for immune clearance in ITP. Reduced platelet production may also contribute to the low count.
alt: Three-stage conceptual sequence of an uncoated platelet, antibody-coated platelet and engulfment by a simplified immune-clearance symbol.

rejectedAttempts.reason: Antibody Y stalks touched the platelet surface, implying reversed antigen-binding orientation. Replace Ys with explicitly abstract marker tabs.

review.notes: Full pixel-to-specification review: three stages run left to right; abstract teal tabs mark the platelet surface and avoid incorrect antibody-domain orientation. A geometric C surrounds the marked platelet; no spleen, organ or tissue is drawn. Reduced production is explicitly acknowledged. The first Y-shaped attempt was rejected and is not used.
